messages:
incident-bot: PRIORITY 1 alert — multiple runtime containers in us-west1 are crashlooping on SIGSEGV. Paging the on-call rotation. https://pd.redwood.example/inc/INC-9231 :rotating_light:

sara: saw this come in, i'm on it. which model fleet?

matt: looks like /models/gpt-medium-v2 on pool-gpu-a (nc1) — 6 pods restarting repeatedly. kube events show OOM + SIGSEGV alternating.

elaine: reprod hint from logs: segfault happens during KV cache restore on load for long context requests. stack contains vllm::kv_cache::restore and a custom fused kernel in /opt/runtime/lib/libkernel.so

javier: pasting recent container log snippet:

```
2026-03-14T22:01:12.345Z ERROR runtime: signal 11 (SIGSEGV), address 0x7ffdeadbeef
2026-03-14T22:01:12.346Z ERROR runtime: backtrace:
  #0  0x7f4a8c1a4 in vllm::kv_cache::restore
  #1  0x7f4a8be22 in vllm::engine::load_state
  #2  0x55f4b0 in main
  CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS during cudaMemcpy
  fused_kernel_init at /opt/runtime/lib/libkernel.so (+0x12af0)
```

javier: also seeing repeated CUDA errors a minute before segfaults: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` — could be bad pointer in fused kernel.

sara: immediate mitigation plan: 1) prevent new traffic to affected pods 2) scale-failed-service to 0 replicas 3) route traffic to fallback model variant (gpt-medium-v2-compat) 4) drain and cordon problematic node until we have debug info.

matt: executing now. `kubectl -n serving scale deploy/model-gpt-medium-v2 --replicas=0` -> succeeded.

deploy-bot: routed 85% of production requests for route /text.generate to fallback cluster (fallback-rw) per runbook.

elaine: for analysis we should capture a core + nvcrashdump. Run `sudo coredumpctl --output=core.sigsegv dump` on node and `nvidia-bug-report.sh` (collect with care).

javier: i've pulled one crash container image and ran `gdb` locally — the crash originates in `fused_kernel_init` path that is only used when REDWOOD_ENABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=1. Could be our custom kernel.

sara: temporary config toggle: setting env `REDWOOD_ENABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=0` for the deployment to cause runtime to fall back to non-fused kernels. matt, can you patch the deployment template and rollout?

matt: patch applied: `kubectl -n serving set env deploy/model-gpt-medium-v2 REDWOOD_ENABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=0` then scaled to 3 replicas on fallback cluster. Pods came up cleanly on fallback.

javier: after toggle, no segfaults in new pods for 30m. older nodes still rebooting due to oom/segfaults at kernel level.

cs-rep: cs-team — impacted customers: AcmeCorp, BrightApps, and CustomerX saw 5-15% increased 5xx on text.generate from 21:55-22:25 PST. We sent status update to Acme support.

elaine: root cause hypothesis: a recent change to fused-kernel memory path introduced a bad pointer when restoring large KV caches; this manifests as CUDA illegal mem access then SIGSEGV. Kernel only used when `REDWOOD_ENABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=1`.

sara: severity call: S1 (production impacting, partial outage for some customers). Incident lead: sara. Action owner for runtime kernel rollback: elaine. Postmortem owner: matt.

matt: short-term: continue running with fused kernels disabled globally for gpt-medium-v2 fleet; schedule canary for a patched kernel tomorrow.

elaine: collecting core dumps + heap traces now, will push symbols to internal S3 at s3://redwood-incident/INC-9231/cores/ . Also creating a debug build with sanitizers to reproduce in CI.

javier: to reduce blast radius we patched autoscaler to maintain 1 spare fallback node per AZ (kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -p '{"spare_nodes":1}')

incident-bot: Incident INC-9231 assigned to sara, severity S1, timeline started 2026-03-14T22:01:12Z. PagerDuty: https://pd.redwood.example/inc/INC-9231

sara: handing off to night oncall (night-oncall) in 40m. summary: crashloops caused by fused-kernel path -> disabled fused kernels; traffic routed to fallback cluster; affected customers notified; collecting cores + nv-dumps; postmortem owners assigned.

night-oncall: ack — i'll monitor for 3 hours. please add any runbook links and the debug artifact locations.

matt: runbook links: https://wiki.redwood/infrastructure/incidents/llm-runtime-crashloops and debug artifacts: s3://redwood-incident/INC-9231/ (cores, nvbugreports, logs).

elaine: next steps for tomorrow: reproduce with sanitizer build, validate kernel patches, run canary with traffic shaping (10% -> 50% -> 100%), and add automated check to fail activation if `nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo` reports >95% commit spike during KV restore.

cs-rep: update we sent to AcmeCorp: "We routed traffic to a compatible variant and applied a temporary configuration change. No customer data was exposed; functionality restored for most customers. Incident lead will follow up with a detailed postmortem."

sara: adding retro items: improve canary coverage for fused kernels, add preflight memory-check for KV restore, better alerting to differentiate OOM vs CUDA_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS, and a rollback playbook for kernel toggles.

night-oncall: taking ownership. assigned to incident in PD. I'll update status channel if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:

sara: thanks team — marking this thread for postmortem. closing active mitigations.
